key_insight: Causal discovery links steel alloying, sheet thickness, and electrode tip diameter to distinct resistance spot-welding signal patterns.
engineering_relevance: These relationships could support more physically interpretable weld monitoring across heterogeneous materials, thicknesses, and electrode configurations.
method: Apply a two-phase causal discovery framework to multicollinear stack-up configurations.
Use time-series clustering to characterize process-signal morphology.
Identify dependencies involving alloying, thickness, tip diameter, and internal faying surfaces.
evidence_signal: Analysis of 15,096 representative profiles derived from over 1.8 million welds found that reducing tip diameter from 8 to 6 mm increased the initial resistance peak by 9%.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish prospective weld-quality improvements or validation on unseen production configurations.
paper_title: Causal discovery of signal morphology drivers in steel resistance spot welding: a high-dimensional data analysis
